en: The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Seal of the Arm of the Victorious Banner, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavān was on the summit of Mount Kailāsa, among the celestial beings, sages, and gods.
In the palace,
he was together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus,
as well as immeasurable and innumerable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Mañjuśrī Bhadrapāla was the leader among the sixteen great beings,
together with all the devas, humans, asuras, and others.
With the Great Brahmā King as their leader,
they were surrounded on all sides by an immeasurable multitude.
At that time, the World-Honored One dwelt in right mindfulness and wisdom.
He preached the subtle and wondrous Dharma for the great assembly.
At that time, the Great Brahma King, leading the hosts of devas,
asuras, and others, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet.
With palms joined in reverence, they stood before the Tathāgata and addressed the Buddha together, saying: "World-Honored One, in the past,
for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings..."
Seeking to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment,
he attained equal and right awakening through a mind perfumed by compassionate vows.
Possessing great supernormal powers and great compassion, he [is]...
Why is it that we currently see various sentient beings fallen into the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals,
as well as among humans and gods, undergoing all manner of intense suffering?
Having failed to employ skillful means to rescue and deliver them, he prayed with compassion:
"May they be granted liberation from their suffering and distress.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara also led forth immeasurable mantra-holding celestial seers (*ṛṣi*).
They prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, joined their palms in reverence,
and standing before the Tathāgata, they addressed him together, saying:
"We pray that you will out of compassion for all sentient beings..."
He revealed the skillful methods for extracting one from suffering and hardship.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the two great beings and their retinues:
"All of you, take your seats."
Out of compassion for all sentient beings, I shall now briefly explain the skillful method for extracting them from suffering and hardship.
You should listen attentively and reflect deeply upon it: there is a great dhāraṇī named "Victorious Banner Arm Seal."
If one constantly recites and keeps [this] in mind, one can extinguish the five heinous crimes, the ten evil deeds, and other such offenses;
one shall never again undergo rebirth in the various evil realms,
nor suffer any of the extreme miseries found among humans and devas.
Those who constantly uphold this will obtain wealth and status in the present life;
in future lives, they will be born into noble families and experience all manner of happiness as they desire manifest before them.
One shall constantly encounter all Buddhas and attain the recollection of past lives,
continuing until reaching unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
The dhāraṇī is as follows:
Kala kala kili kili kulu kulu.
Sara sara sire sire sulū sulū.
Sarvabuddhaparigrahaṃ dala dala.
Sarvadharmāṅgamukhe jvale jvale sarvasaṃghādhiṣṭhite.
Valoka valoka anīka buddha koṭi vāstika.
Cina cina sarvakarmavaraṇāni me moṣaya sarvasattvānāñ ca.
Sarvabodhanisrava-dhukha-padayebṛta bṛta.
Ḍaṭṭha ḍaṭṭha naṭṭha naṭṭha kaṭṭha kaṭṭha.
*Sābhūṭaye sābhūṭaye sarvavīranapāyottarāṇi svāhā*.
O son of good family, this is the *dhāraṇī* of the "Victorious Banner Arm Seal."
This has been taught by all the Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Out of compassion for all sentient beings, and because of your request, I too shall now speak it for the sake of the assembly.
Good son, the appearance of the Buddhas in the world is extremely difficult to encounter;
obtaining a human body is even more difficult than that;
and hearing this divine mantra is yet more difficult still.
If there are sons or daughters of good family who are able to correctly receive and uphold [this teaching], that is already difficult to find;
how much more so to transcribe it and diligently recite and contemplate it!
And as for those who encourage others to receive and uphold [this teaching]:
"Good son, I recall that in the past,
I was in the presence of various Buddhas, such as Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha and Bhaisajyarāja."
Having heard this divine mantra, by receiving, upholding, reading, reciting, and correctly explaining it to others,
one shall thereby realize unsurpassed bodhi. Therefore,
you all should diligently study it accordingly.
He exhorted all sentient beings to receive, uphold, read, and recite it,
so that they might be liberated from suffering and calamity and attain supreme benefit and happiness.
When the Bhagavān had finished speaking this sutra, [the assembly rejoiced].
The Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, the Bodhisattva Bhadrapāla, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
the Great Brahmā King, and all the devas, humans, asuras, and others.
When the entire great assembly heard what the Buddha had spoken, they were all filled with great joy; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
*The Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Victorious Banner Arm Seal*.
